この著者の方御本人は存じ上げておりませんが、この方の周囲にいる方々（著者の大学院時代の指導者など）は、文中に援用している酒井隆史さんも含めそれなりによく存じ上げております。ですので、どういった意図でこうした記事をお書きになるのか、その問題点も含め、大まかなところは理解しているつもりです。

こうした見解に対し、過度な政治的議論や感情論に走らず、あくまで理論的に対応していくことを、新設されたこのチャンネルの役目の一つなっていったらいいなと個人的に思っています。それがプルラリティ的な「DD（2030）の哲学」の生産に繋がるのではないでしょうか？

attachments.fallback: Zenodo: Dynamic Tools for Digital Democracy: From Static Aggregation to Process Design
attachments.text: Digital democracy practitioners have built important infrastructure for civic participation over the past decade. Platforms like vTaiwan, Polis, and Decidim have demonstrated that technology can facilitate large-scale deliberation. Yet these initiatives consistently encounter similar challenges: difficulty scaling beyond pilot projects, outcomes that fail to translate into sustained change, and occasional unintended consequences such as polarization or capture by motivated minorities. This paper identifies a common root cause: current theoretical frameworks—inherited from equilibrium-based approaches exemplified by Anderson's 'More is Different' (1972) and formalized in Landau-Ginzburg theory—describe static states rather than dynamic processes. These frameworks can compare endpoints but cannot represent transitions, instabilities, or path dependence. We introduce an alternative: the Stuart-Landau equation, a mathematical framework that describes how order emerges dynamically through critical transitions. This framework enables practitioners to detect approaching instabilities, design temporal structures for deliberation, and understand when and why democratic processes succeed or fail. Rather than replacing existing work, this tool extends it: the infrastructure already built becomes more powerful when guided by dynamic theory.
attachments.title: Dynamic Tools for Digital Democracy: From Static Aggregation to Process Design

attachments.fallback: Zenodo: Description Without Causation: A Cognitive Approach to Structural Universality
attachments.text: Causation in the metaphysical sense—a primitive relation of necessitation between events—does notexist. What we call “causation” conflates three distinct phenomena. Constraint satisfaction is astructural relation, real and mind-independent, derivable as a theorem. A cognitive label is an attributiongenerated by prediction error minimization when the brain encounters highly predictable regularities.Retrospective narrative is the causal story imposed after convergence from phase transitions whosemicro-level dynamics do not compress into sequential causal accounts. The first is not causation—it ismathematics. Metaphysical causation reduces to the latter two—neural projection and narrativeconstruction—neither of which has a mind-independent referent. The Stuart-Landau equation, whosemathematical structure recurs across physically distinct domains without causal mechanism, providesthe central evidence. The Order Emergence Structure (OES) formalizes the constraint morphismsconnecting these domains, grounded in the analyticity of physical dynamics (Sophia, 2026), and servesas an axiomatic foundation from which “causal” claims are derivable as theorems. This frameworkdissolves the apparent tension between Humean skepticism and Kantian realism about causation: Humeand Norton are correct that the primitive relation has no referent; Kant is correct that structural relationsare real—but wrong to call them causation. For systems exhibiting order through attractive interactions,“why” questions terminate not in deeper causes but in axiomatic derivation.
attachments.title: Description Without Causation: A Cognitive Approach to Structural Universality

attachments.fallback: Zenodo: Amid Turning Points, Futures Are Designed, Not Awaited A Field Report on the Verification Cost Reversal
attachments.text: For decades, futures scholars have warned that Post-Normal Times would arrive—an era where uncertainty, rapid change, and systemic complexity would overwhelm traditional prediction. Sardar described it. Miller developed Futures Literacy to navigate it. Ramos and colleagues built frameworks for Triple-A Governance to respond to it. This paper argues that Post-Normal Times have arrived, and offers a field report from someone working at the intersection of AI and organizational transformation. The specific trigger is what I call the verification cost reversal. For most of human history, producing plausible falsehoods was cheap while verification was expensive—creating demand for authority-based knowledge structures. Now verification is cheap, maintaining deception is expensive, and credibility loss is irreversible. Combined with the automation of cognitive routine labor, this reversal is displacing authority structures and knowledge work at unprecedented speed. In Post-Normal Times terminology, this is a Black Jellyfish: a known threat whose cascading, systemic effects are underestimated while attention focuses elsewhere. Much of futures discourse remains fixated on the Black Swan of artificial general intelligence—scanning distant horizons— while Black Jellyfish drift through familiar waters. The transformation is not approaching. It has arrived. This paper synthesizes insights from Bell's foundational vision, Sardar's Post-Normal Times framework, Miller's Futures Literacy, and Ramos's anticipatory governance work to understand what is happening and what it demands. The answer aligns with what these scholars have long advocated: continuous updating, adaptive capacity, and design rather than prediction. The future is not awaited—it is designed through iterative engagement with changing conditions. It is time to stop scanning the horizon and start addressing what is already in the water.
attachments.title: Amid Turning Points, Futures Are Designed, Not Awaited A Field Report on the Verification Cost Reversal

attachments.fallback: Zenodo: Why Eighteen? Military Origins and Administrative Logic of Age-Based Citizenship
attachments.text: Modern nation-states exhibit a striking convergence in their age-based institutional thresholds:voting rights at 18, full criminal responsibility between 18-22, and mandatory educationconcluding around 18. This paper argues that these thresholds derive not from principledconsiderations of cognitive development or democratic theory, but from the military logic of thenineteenth-century nation-state, which required citizens whose "consumable value" to thestate–their capacity to be expended in warfare–peaked in early adulthood. Drawing on James C.Scott's concept of state legibility, I demonstrate how the construction of the "homogeneouscitizen" served administrative convenience rather than individual flourishing. I furtherdocument how protective regulations originally designed as ceilings against exploitation–suchas the eight-hour workday and retirement age–have been inverted into normative floors thatexclude those who cannot conform. Finally, I examine an asymmetric framework for politicalparticipation that distinguishes stakeholder rights from accountability requirements, and identifydimensions for institutional reconsideration–while acknowledging that specific reforms requiredemocratic deliberation this analysis can inform but not replace.

昨日、「雑談」チャンネルのほうで西尾さんが取り上げていたこの記事、平野啓一郎やら元日経BP編集長やら（名前は忘れたが昨年の参議院選時に「みらい」と揉めた人？）やらがX上で好意的に取り上げてまして、随分と話題になっているようですね。

この著者の方御本人は存じ上げておりませんが、この方の周囲にいる方々（著者の大学院時代の指導者など）は、文中に援用している酒井隆史さんも含めそれなりによく存じ上げております。ですので、どういった意図でこうした記事をお書きになるのか、その問題点も含め、大まかなところは理解しているつもりです。

こうした見解に対し、過度な政治的議論や感情論に走らず、あくまで理論的に対応していくことを、新設されたこのチャンネルの役目の一つなっていったらいいなと個人的に思っています。それがプルラリティ的な「DD（2030）の哲学」の生産に繋がるのではないでしょうか？
